corpus.description: OWASP Benchmark for Java 1.2: 2,740 servlet test cases across 11 vulnerability categories, each labelled as a real vulnerability or a false-positive trap.
SYNTHETIC line-labelled secrets corpus generated by benchmark/synthetic_secrets.py (seeded). Random values in real credential formats plus realistic decoys; nothing in it was ever a live credential.
Lock files / manifests generated by benchmark/sca_corpus.py pinning known-vulnerable versions in five ecosystems; truth = OSV advisories per package@version, snapshotted in benchmark/sca_truth.json.

OpenSSF CVE Benchmark: metadata for 223 real JavaScript/TypeScript CVEs (repository, last vulnerable commit with the vulnerable line labelled, fix commit). benchmark/ossf_cve.py fetches the labelled files at both commits from raw.githubusercontent.com.
corpus.license: MIT (metadata); each CVE's code under its own project's licence (scanned locally, not redistributed)

corpus.description: OWASP Benchmark for Python 0.1: 1,230 Flask test cases across 14 vulnerability categories, each labelled as a real vulnerability or a false-positive trap. Upstream calls 0.1 a preliminary release and publishes it as the head of main, so a commit is pinned.
